Let \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).  Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, ass:frechet-covariance-domain, and ass:product-coupling-zero,
\[
h(c)=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.
\]
If \(c_L<c_U\), minimization of \(w(B)\) is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\): as functions of a formal endpoint-gain pair \((x_L,x_U)\), the two loss criteria are not related by a constant independent of \((x_L,x_U)\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
 E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
 \qquad A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
Def:moment-matrix gives \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\).  The value at zero is well typed by ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain.  For each unit, mutual exclusivity gives
\[
 \Omega_{i,n+i}=\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(D_{i,1},D_{i,0})
 =-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}.
\]
Exposure positivity permits division, and symmetry gives
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)
 =2\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\Omega_{i,n+i}}{\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}}=-2n.
\]
Therefore
\[
 h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_{\mathrm{HT}}Q(c)\}
 =h(0)-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)
 =h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Substitution into def:gain-loss and def:robust-objective proves the displayed formula for \(w(B)\).

For the non-equivalence, set \(a_e=2c_e/n\) and, for a formal gain pair \(x=(x_L,x_U)\), define
\[
 \Phi(x)=\max\{a_L-x_L,a_U-x_U\},
 \qquad \Psi(x)=-\min\{x_L,x_U\}.
\]
If \(\Phi=\Psi+K\) for a constant independent of \(x\), evaluation at \((t,0)\) and letting \(t\to\infty\) gives \(K=a_U\), whereas evaluation at \((0,t)\) gives \(K=a_L\).  Thus no such constant exists when \(c_L<c_U\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\) and both regular classes are nonempty, then
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
\le
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
=
\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
If the right-hand infimum is attained by some \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_Z\), then there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that, for every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
This value transfer concerns only the nonsingular ordinary-inverse projective class \(\mathcal B_Z\), not singular or pseudoinverse bases or Zhao's larger unquotiented domain.
statements.justification: This is the exact converse-value transfer justified by the compact projective exhaustion.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates does not introduce a normalized threshold family or prove convergence of its optimization values as the threshold vanishes.
statements.consumer: A solver can report how its fixed regularity threshold approximates the best value over the entire nonsingular ordinary-inverse projective repair.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\), then \(\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}\), so minimizing the same continuous loss over the larger compact set proves the first inequality.  Prop:kappa-exhaustion gives \(\mathcal B_Z=\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa\).  The infimum of a function over a union is the infimum of the infima over its nonempty members, whence
\[
 \inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
 =\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
 \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\]
If \(B_Z^\star\) attains the left side, prop:kappa-exhaustion supplies \(\kappa_0>0\) with \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_0}\).  For \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
 \inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
 \le\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
 \le w(B_Z^\star)
 =\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
This proves equality and concerns only the ordinary-inverse class. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility hold.  The primary minimax correspondence is nonempty and satisfies the unconditional weak worst-copula dominance certificate
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]
Strict inequality is not universal and requires a separate lawful witness.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Ass:kappa-feasibility makes \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) nonempty, and prop:kappa-exhaustion makes it compact.  Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  On this class, \(S_B\succeq n\kappa I_2\), so inversion is continuous and bounded.  Hence \(B\mapsto g_B(0)\), both endpoint losses, and \(w(B)\) are continuous and attain their extrema.  Thus \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_0\) are nonempty.  For arbitrary \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0\), the defining minimization gives
\[
 w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_0).
\]
Taking the supremum and infimum gives the displayed certificate.

Strictness is not universal: for any lawful design, take \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\).  Then \(Q(0)=0\), hence \(g_B(0)=\ell_B(0)=w(B)=0\) for every feasible basis.

For positioning only, the in-repository results \(\texttt{exp\_bipartite\_minimax\_design\_v1/thm:hetero-envelope}\) and \(\texttt{exp\_bipartite\_minimax\_design\_v1/thm:convex-design}\) choose heterogeneous assignment probabilities for a conservative graph-only H\'ajek envelope.  Here \(\nu\) is fixed and the decision is a control-variate span under copula ambiguity; no mathematical step above is borrowed from those results. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) and suppose that, for some \(\eta>0\),
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}\ge\eta.
\]
For every sequence \((\xi_j)_{j\ge1}\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) converging to \(\xi_0\) in the relative topology of def:lawful-instance-class,
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)\ge\Delta(\xi_0).
\]
statements.justification: This quantitative lower-semicontinuity lemma is the reusable step that turns an exact optimizer-wide slack certificate into a uniform dominance margin.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals supplies continuity of the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence; the new step propagates that continuity through the moving regular projective feasible set and both optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: The triangle neighborhood corollary uses the lemma to preserve half of the exact rational separation margin.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(\xi_j=(\nu_j,F_{1j},F_{0j})\to\xi_0\).  Use normalized representatives in the fixed compact product of spheres modulo signs.  Because the assignment space is finite, total-variation convergence of \(\nu_j\) implies entrywise convergence \(\Pi_j\to\Pi_0\) and \(\Omega_j\to\Omega_0\).  Exposure positivity at \(\xi_0\) implies that all relevant diagonal entries stay uniformly away from zero eventually, so \(\Pi_j^{-1}\to\Pi_0^{-1}\).

Wasserstein convergence on \([0,1]\) implies weak convergence and convergence of first and second moments.  Lem:restricted-marginal-extrema-continuity, applied to \(\varphi(y_1,y_0)=y_1y_0\), gives convergence of the minimum and maximum cross moments over the coupling sets.  Subtracting the convergent products of marginal means yields
\[
 c_{Lj}\to c_{L0},\qquad c_{Uj}\to c_{U0}.
\]
Def:moment-matrix then gives \(Q_j(c_{ej})\to Q_0(c_{e0})\) for \(e\in\{L,U\}\).

For a normalized basis \(B\), put
\[
 \rho(\xi,B)=\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega(\xi)B\}.
\]
This function is jointly continuous.  On every set \(\rho\ge\kappa\), exposure positivity and the inverse bound \(\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}\) make \(g_{B,\xi}(c_e)\), \(\ell_{B,\xi}(c_e)\), \(w_\xi(B)\), and \(g_{B,\xi}(0)\) jointly continuous.

Choose \(B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\).  The assumed slack gives \(\rho(\xi_0,B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}})\ge\kappa+\eta\); hence this fixed representative is feasible for all large \(j\).  Therefore
\[
 \limsup_j v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)
 \le\lim_j w_{\xi_j}(B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}})
 =v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0). \tag{1}
\]

For each \(j\), choose \(B_{0j}\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)\) minimizing \(w_{\xi_j}\) over that optimizer set.  Compactness supplies a subsequence, still indexed by \(j\), with \(B_{0j}\to\bar B_0\).  Closedness of \(\rho\ge\kappa\) makes \(\bar B_0\) feasible at \(\xi_0\).  Choose any \(C_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).  Its slack makes it feasible for all large \(j\), and empirical optimality gives
\[
 g_{B_{0j},\xi_j}(0)\ge g_{C_0,\xi_j}(0).
\]
Passing to the limit shows that \(\bar B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).  Joint continuity then yields
\[
 \liminf_j\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B)
 =w_{\xi_0}(\bar B_0)
 \ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B). \tag{2}
\]
The subsequence was chosen to realize the lower limit, so (2) holds for the original sequence.  Finally, def:dominance-gap and (1)--(2) imply
\[
 \liminf_j\Delta(\xi_j)
 \ge \inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)
 =\Delta(\xi_0).
\]
All inversions, moving-feasible-set comparisons, and boundary passages have thus been justified by positivity, compactness, and the stated optimizer-wide slack. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For the explicit triangle instance \(\xi_0\) and \(\kappa=1/8\) in thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) containing \(\xi_0\) such that
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac{\delta}{2}=\frac{2456}{39525}
\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U),
\]
where \(\delta=4912/39525\).  Consequently, for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\), every \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), and every \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)\),
\[
w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})<w_\xi(B_0).
\]
statements.justification: The explicit witness becomes a nondegenerate region of lawful designs and marginals, with a retained rational performance margin.
statements.gap: Neither Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates nor general dependence-robust optimization results give a strict full-correspondence comparison between the minimax and zero-covariance basis rules on an open family of network experiments.
statements.consumer: Nearby lawful network experiments inherit the guarantee that every minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The triangle certificate gives \(\Delta(\xi_0)=\delta>0\) and optimizer-wide slack \(\eta>0\).  By thm:relative-open-persistence there is a relative-open neighborhood with positive gap.  To retain half the exact margin, argue by contradiction: if every neighborhood contained \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) with \(\Delta(\xi_j)\le\delta/2\), lem:dominance-gap-lower-semicontinuity would give
\[
 \delta=\Delta(\xi_0)\le\liminf_j\Delta(\xi_j)\le\delta/2,
\]
impossible.  Hence some relative-open \(\mathcal U\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi)>\delta/2\).  For any indicated optimizers,
\[
 w_\xi(B_0)-w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
 \ge\inf_{C_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_\xi(C_0)
 -\sup_{C\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_\xi(C)
 =\Delta(\xi)>\delta/2,
\]
which proves the strict comparison. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every rational signed pivot-chart box, intersection with the normalized feasible set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is an existential semialgebraic question.  More explicitly, sphere feasibility, chart and box restrictions, and \(S_B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\) are finitely many polynomial equalities and weak inequalities with rational or real-algebraic coefficients; for
\[
 S_B-n\kappa I_2=\begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix},
\]
the matrix inequality is exactly \(u\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(uz-v^2\ge0\).  Cylindrical algebraic decomposition therefore terminates with either an exact real-algebraic feasible sample or a finite infeasibility certificate, including when feasibility occurs only on the equality boundary.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The entries of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\) are quadratic polynomials in the \(2n\) coordinates of \((b_1,b_0)\), with rational or real-algebraic coefficients.  The two sphere conditions are polynomial equalities, while rational box and signed pivot-chart restrictions are polynomial weak inequalities.  For a symmetric two-by-two matrix,
\[
 \begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix}\succeq0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u\ge0,\ z\ge0,\ uz-v^2\ge0.
\]
Applying this identity to \(S_B-n\kappa I_2\) includes equality at the regularity boundary exactly.

Thus chart-box feasibility is an existential first-order formula over the real closed field of real-algebraic numbers.  The Collins EVAL/ELIM result supplies a quantifier-free equivalent.  Its DECOMP construction partitions the finitely many polynomial sign conditions into finitely described cells with algebraic sample points; recursive projection lowers the variable count and therefore terminates after finitely many stages.  Exact algebraic-number isolation evaluates every sign at each sample.  A sign-compatible sample satisfying the formula is an exact feasible point; if no cell sample satisfies it, the finite sign-invariant decomposition is an infeasibility certificate.  These are the adaptations to the present sphere, box, and positive-semidefinite constraints; none is asserted by the cited leaf alone. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Define \(\iota:\mathcal B_Z\to\mathcal B_Z^+\) by \(\iota([B])=[B]_+\).  This map is a well-defined bijection from \(\mathcal B_Z\) onto
\[
 \{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)=2\}.
\]
For every \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\) and every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\),
\[
 g_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=g_B(c),
 \qquad \ell_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=\ell_B(c),
 \qquad w^+(\iota(B))=w(B).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\), then \(S_B\succ0\), so both columns are nonzero and \(\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=2\).  Independent nonzero rescaling is the equivalence relation used by the ordinary projective class and by the rank-two stratum of the novel completion.  Hence \([B]\mapsto[B]_+\) is well defined and injective.

Conversely, let \([C]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) have \(\operatorname{rank}(C^{\top}\Omega C)=2\).  Its two columns are nonzero, and \(C^{\top}\Omega C\) is a two-by-two positive-semidefinite matrix of rank two, hence positive definite.  Def:zhao-basis-class therefore defines \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and \(\iota([C])=[C]_+\).  This proves surjectivity onto the stated stratum.

On rank two the Moore--Penrose inverse equals the ordinary inverse.  Substitution into def:published-pseudoinverse-loss and def:gain-loss gives equality of the gains for every feasible \(c\); subtracting from the common uncontrolled variance gives equality of endpoint losses, and taking the maximum gives \(w^+(\iota(B))=w(B)\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), set \(A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\) and \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\).  Every \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) satisfies
\[
 g_B^+(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e),
 \qquad P_B=Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top},
\]
where \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), \(A_e\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  On rank two, \([B]_+=\iota([C])\) for a unique \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and the gains and losses agree.  If \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\), then for every singular \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) there is a sequence \([B_j]\in\mathcal B_Z\) such that
\[
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}w(B_j)\le w^+(B).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(e\in\{L,U\}\).  Def:moment-matrix gives \(Q(c_e)\succeq0\), and exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  Congruence gives
\[
 A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\succeq0. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(S_B=Z_B^{\top}Z_B\), cyclicity of trace gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 n^2g_B^+(c_e)
 &=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}A_eZ_B\right]\\
 &=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}A_e\right]
 =\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e).
 \end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
The singular-value decomposition of \(Z_B\) shows that \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\) and has rank \(\operatorname{rank}(Z_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  The rank-two assertion follows from lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification.

For the approximation, first choose an actual block-separable representative \(B^\circ\) of the singular completion class and an actual representative \(C^\circ\) of any \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\).  Only after these choices define
\[
 B_t^\circ=B^\circ+tC^\circ.
\]
It remains block separable, and
\[
 p(t)=\det\!\left\{(Z_{B^\circ}+tZ_{C^\circ})^{\top}(Z_{B^\circ}+tZ_{C^\circ})\right\}
\]
is a polynomial with positive leading coefficient \(\det(Z_{C^\circ}^{\top}Z_{C^\circ})\).  It has finitely many roots.  Choose \(t_j\downarrow0\) away from them, independently normalize the two nonzero columns of \(B_{t_j}^\circ\), and only then return to the ordinary quotient, obtaining \([B_j]\in\mathcal B_Z\).  Column normalization does not change the associated projector.

Along a subsequence the rank-two projectors converge to \(P_\infty\).  If \(x=Z_{B^\circ}u\), then \((Z_{B^\circ}+t_jZ_{C^\circ})u\to x\) and belongs to the range of \(P_{B_j}\).  Hence
\[
 \lVert P_{B_j}x-x\rVert
 \le2\lVert x-(Z_{B^\circ}+t_jZ_{C^\circ})u\rVert\to0.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{range}(P_B)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(P_\infty)\) and \(P_\infty-P_B\succeq0\).  Equations (1)--(2) imply simultaneously at both endpoints
\[
 \lim_jg_{B_j}(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_\infty A_e)
 \ge g_B^+(c_e).
\]
The uncontrolled term is basis independent, so \(\limsup_j\ell_{B_j}(c_e)\le\ell_B^+(c_e)\); taking the maximum proves \(\limsup_jw(B_j)\le w^+(B)\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every rational or real-algebraic input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the algebraic projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a locally checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
 L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
The incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\) has finite real-algebraic coordinates, including when every feasible point lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  The checker verifies only CAD sign certificates, algebraic feasibility, outward objective bounds, rational norm and diameter records, chart cover, pruning inequalities, and mesh; the displayed facts about \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are mathematical consequences.  Along every \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and meshes converge to zero.  No uniform complexity bound or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
\emph{Step 1: compact algebraic feasible set.}
Use normalized representatives and put
\[
 K_\kappa=\{(b_1,b_0):\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
 \ S_B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\}.
\]
Ass:kappa-feasibility makes this set nonempty, and prop:kappa-exhaustion makes its quotient compact.  On a radius-\(\sqrt n\) sphere some coordinate has absolute value at least one, so the finitely many signed pivot regions \(\{\pm b_j\ge1\}\) cover each projective factor.  Retaining the sphere equations and pivot sign gives a finite semialgebraic chart cover.  Lem:algebraic-box-feasibility-cad decides each rational chart-box intersection with \(K_\kappa\) and returns an algebraic point when nonempty, including on the equality boundary.

\emph{Step 2: an effective uniform loss modulus.}
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), put
\[
 R_e=\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega,
 \quad S(B)=B^{\top}\Omega B,
 \quad T_e(B)=B^{\top}R_eB.
\]
Exact algebraic sign evaluation and exposure positivity provide positive lower bounds for the diagonal entries of \(\Pi\) and for \(\kappa\), and rational upper bounds \(M_\Omega\ge\lVert\Omega\rVert_2\) and \(M_e\ge\lVert R_e\rVert_2\).  Every normalized block matrix satisfies \(\lVert B\rVert_F=\sqrt{2n}\).  If \(d=\lVert B-C\rVert_F\), then
\[
 \lVert S(B)-S(C)\rVert_2\le K_Sd,
 \qquad \lVert T_e(B)-T_e(C)\rVert_2\le K_{T,e}d,
\]
where \(K_S=2\sqrt{2n}M_\Omega\) and \(K_{T,e}=2\sqrt{2n}M_e\).  On \(K_\kappa\),
\[
 S(B)\succeq n\kappa I_2,
 \qquad \lVert S(B)^{-1}\rVert_2\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\]
The resolvent identity and \(\lvert\operatorname{tr}(XY)\rvert\le2\lVert X\rVert_2\lVert Y\rVert_2\) give
\[
 \lvert g_B(c_e)-g_C(c_e)\rvert\le L_ed,
 \quad
 L_e=n^{-2}\left\{\frac{2K_{T,e}}{n\kappa}
 +\frac{4nM_eK_S}{(n\kappa)^2}\right\}.
\]
The uncontrolled term is basis independent and the maximum is one-Lipschitz, hence
\[
 \lvert w(B)-w(C)\rvert\le L\lVert B-C\rVert_F,
 \qquad L=\max\{L_L,L_U\}. \tag{1}
\]
Algebraic isolation supplies a recorded rational \(\overline L\ge L\).

\emph{Step 3: finite exhaustive depth.}
Choose rational \(\alpha>0\) with \(4\alpha<\varepsilon\).  Uniform bisection reaches a finite depth at which every chart box \(C\) has rational diameter bound \(d_C\) with
\[
 d_C\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad \overline Ld_C\le\alpha. \tag{2}
\]
There are finitely many boxes.  CAD certifies each empty box and returns an exact algebraic sample \(B_C\) for each feasible box.  Algebraic isolation terminates with rationals \(\underline q_C,\overline q_C\) satisfying
\[
 w(B_C)-\alpha\le\underline q_C\le w(B_C)
 \le\overline q_C\le w(B_C)+\alpha. \tag{3}
\]
By (1)--(2),
\[
 \lambda_C:=\underline q_C-\overline Ld_C
 \le\inf_{B\in C\cap K_\kappa}w(B). \tag{4}
\]
Let \(U_\varepsilon=\min_C\overline q_C\), choose the corresponding algebraic sample as \(B_\varepsilon\), and set \(L_\varepsilon=\min_C\lambda_C\).  Compactness supplies a minimizer \(B^\star\).  A box containing it and (1)--(4) imply
\[
 v_{\mathrm{mm}}-2\alpha\le L_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}
 \le w(B_\varepsilon)\le U_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\alpha.
\]
Thus \(U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon\le4\alpha<\varepsilon\).

\emph{Step 4: outer boxes and local checking.}
Prune a feasible box only if \(\lambda_C>U_\varepsilon\).  By (4) such a box cannot contain a minimizer, whereas a box containing a minimizer has \(\lambda_C\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le U_\varepsilon\).  Let \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) be the quotient image of all retained feasible boxes.  Then \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and (2) gives \(h_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\).

The checker receives only finite CAD sign records, algebraic feasible coordinates, rational interval inclusions, norm and Lipschitz bounds, chart cover, pruning comparisons, and mesh.  The inequalities concerning \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are consequences of those records, not inputs to the checker.  Every stage terminates after finitely many algebraic operations and subdivisions.  Repeating the construction for \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) makes both the certified value gap and mesh tend to zero. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:frechet-covariance-domain hold and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  For the novel Moore--Penrose completion of def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain,
\[
 v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 =\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
 =\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
   \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\]
Writing \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\) for the fixed-threshold argmin, the rank-two completion minimizers are exactly
\[
 \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\cap\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
 =\iota\!\left(
 \bigcup_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,
 \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+}}
 \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\right).
\]
Possible singular ties are retained as the separate stratum
\[
 \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\setminus\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
 =\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1,\ w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
No existence of a singular tie is asserted, and no part of this completion is attributed to Zhao.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For every \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification gives \(w^+(\iota(C))=w(C)\).  Since \(\iota(C)\) is feasible in the novel completion,
\[
 v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\le\inf_{C\in\mathcal B_Z}w(C). \tag{1}
\]
Conversely, a rank-two completion class is uniquely \(\iota(C)\), while a singular completion class admits, by lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction, ordinary classes \(C_j\) with \(\limsup_jw(C_j)\le w^+(B)\).  Hence \(\inf_{C\in\mathcal B_Z}w(C)\le w^+(B)\) for every completion class.  Taking the minimum over that class and combining with (1) proves
\[
 v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{C\in\mathcal B_Z}w(C).
\]
Prop:kappa-value-exhaustion gives the second equality.

If a rank-two completion minimizer equals \(\iota(C)\), prop:kappa-exhaustion supplies \(\kappa_C>0\) with \(C\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_C}\).  Then
\[
 v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 \le\min_{A\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_C}}w(A)
 \le w(C)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+,
\]
so \(C\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa_C)\) at a value-attaining threshold.  Conversely, every member of a fixed-threshold argmin whose value is \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) maps under \(\iota\) to a rank-two completion minimizer.  This proves the exact rank-two identity.  The final displayed set in the statement merely partitions the remaining equality set by rank; it retains possible singular ties and asserts no existence. \(\square\)

For the triangle matrices
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
and the endpoint matrices
\[
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad A=\frac{I_3+J_3}{4},
\]
the rank-zero and rank-one strata of the novel Moore--Penrose completion obey the exact bounds
\[
\sup_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)
=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80}
\]
and
\[
\inf_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)
=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
More precisely, rank zero has \(g_B^+(0)=0\) and \(w^+(B)=171/200\).  In rank one, after normalizing the unique nonzero arm vector to squared norm three and writing \(u\) for the squared sum of its coordinates, so \(0\le u\le9\), the focal-only stratum has
\[
g_x^+(c_L)=\frac{1195u+6561}{1200(81-4u)},
\qquad g_x^+(c_U)=\frac{243(49-5u)}{400(81-4u)},
\]
whereas the comparison-only stratum has
\[
g_y^+(c_L)=\frac{1240u+729}{150(4u+243)},
\qquad g_y^+(c_U)=\frac{81(48-5u)}{50(4u+243)}.
\]
These rational formulas, together with \(0\le u\le9\), are an exact semialgebraic certificate for both displayed strict inequalities.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(\mathbf1=\mathbf1_3\).  Simultaneous permutation decomposition into \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\) and \(\mathbf1^\perp\) reduces \(729\Omega\) to
\[
 M_\parallel=\begin{bmatrix}60&96\\96&186\end{bmatrix},
 \qquad M_\perp=\begin{bmatrix}108&-108\\-108&162\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Their leading entries are positive and their determinants are \(1944\) and \(5832\), so \(\Omega\succ0\).  Therefore rank zero means both arm columns vanish, while rank one means exactly one arm column is nonzero.

On the focal-only stratum normalize \(\lVert x\rVert_2^2=3\) and set \(u=(\mathbf1^{\top}x)^2\in[0,9]\).  The scalar Rayleigh quotient from lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction gives
\[
 g_x^+(c_L)=\frac{1195u+6561}{1200(81-4u)},
 \qquad g_x^+(c_U)=\frac{243(49-5u)}{400(81-4u)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 g_x^+(0)=\frac{21141-1225u}{1200(81-4u)},
 \qquad \frac{d}{du}g_x^+(0)=-\frac{4887}{400(4u-81)^2}<0.
\]
Using \(h(c_L)=313/600\) and \(h(c_U)=171/200\), the upper endpoint is always the worse loss and
\[
 \ell_{x,U}=\frac{9(1755-17u)}{400(81-4u)},
 \qquad \frac{d}{du}\ell_{x,U}=\frac{50787}{400(4u-81)^2}>0.
\]
Thus the focal-only maximum zero gain is \(87/400\), and its minimum worst loss is \(39/80\), both at \(u=0\).

On the comparison-only stratum, normalize \(\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3\) and use \(u=(\mathbf1^{\top}y)^2\in[0,9]\).  Direct substitution gives
\[
 g_y^+(c_L)=\frac{1240u+729}{150(4u+243)},
 \qquad g_y^+(c_U)=\frac{81(48-5u)}{50(4u+243)},
\]
and hence
\[
 g_y^+(0)=\frac{25u+12393}{300(4u+243)},
 \qquad \frac{d}{du}g_y^+(0)=-\frac{14499}{100(4u+243)^2}<0,
\]
while the upper endpoint is again worse and
\[
 \ell_{y,U}=\frac{9(256u+2889)}{200(4u+243)},
 \qquad \frac{d}{du}\ell_{y,U}=\frac{113967}{50(4u+243)^2}>0.
\]
Thus the comparison-only extrema are \(17/100\) and \(107/200\).  Rank zero has zero gain and worst loss \(171/200\).  Comparing all three singular cases yields
\[
 \sup_{\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80},
 \qquad
 \inf_{\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
Every denominator is positive on \([0,9]\), so all boundary cases are included. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness whose strict separation survives every singular stratum of the novel Moore--Penrose completion.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized rank-two representatives \(B(x,y)\),
\[
\mathcal A_0=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=\mathbf1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,
\ (\mathbf1^{\top}y)^2=216/55\}.
\]
They are nonempty, lie in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), and satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\quad w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200},
\quad w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432},
\quad \lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}
\]
on the respective equality sets.  Under the rank-two bijection \(\iota:\mathcal B_Z\to\mathcal B_Z^+\), the optimizer sets and values on the full novel completion, including ranks zero and one, are exactly
\[
\mathcal A_0^+=\iota(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\iota(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
\[
\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)=\frac{2613}{8432};
\]
in particular, there are no singular optimizer ties.  Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},\qquad \eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the ordinary and completion full-correspondence gaps and the optimizer-wide regularity slack asserted by def:dominance-gap.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The exact assignment enumeration, endpoint calculation, and rank-two optimization in thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate give the displayed \(\Pi\), \(\Omega\), \(c_L,c_U\), endpoint moment matrices, the full ordinary equality sets, and the values
\[
 \max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
 \qquad w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200},
 \qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
Those same polynomial certificates were derived without using the upper \(\kappa\)-restriction except to license inversion; the displayed \(\Omega\) is positive definite by lem:triangle-completion-singular-strata-certificate, so every rank-two block basis is invertible.  Hence the equality sets are also the complete rank-two equality sets in the novel Moore--Penrose completion.  Lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification transfers them through \(\iota\) without changing gains or losses.

It remains to exclude singular ties, rather than infer their absence from the definition.  Lem:triangle-completion-singular-strata-certificate proves
\[
 \sup_{\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80}
\]
and
\[
 \inf_{\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
Thus no rank-zero or rank-one completion class is a zero-covariance or minimax optimizer, and
\[
 \mathcal A_0^+=\iota(\mathcal A_0),
 \qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\iota(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}})
\]
with the stated values.

Every ordinary optimizer has \(\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=4/27\), while \(\kappa=1/8\).  Exposure positivity and the explicit feasible bases therefore put \(\xi_0\) in \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the full-correspondence differences are
\[
 \delta=\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}=\frac{4912}{39525}>0,
 \qquad \eta=\frac4{27}-\frac18=\frac5{216}>0.
\]
The first equality is preserved by \(\iota\), so it holds in both the ordinary class and its novel completion. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For the explicit triangle instance \(\xi_0\) and \(\kappa=1/8\) in thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) containing \(\xi_0\) such that
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac{\delta}{2}=\frac{2456}{39525}
\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U).
\]
Throughout \(\mathcal U\), the completion optimizer correspondences contain no singular classes and satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_0^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_0(\xi)),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)).
\]
Consequently every ordinary minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula loss than every ordinary zero-covariance optimizer, and every completion minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula loss than every completion zero-covariance optimizer, with each difference exceeding \(\delta/2\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
At \(\xi_0\), thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate gives the ordinary gap \(\delta>0\), optimizer-wide slack \(\eta>0\), and strict singular-stratum gaps
\[
 \frac{31}{80}-\frac{87}{400}=\frac{17}{100}>0,
 \qquad
 \frac{39}{80}-\frac{2613}{8432}=\frac{468}{2635}>0. \tag{1}
\]
Total-variation convergence of the finite assignment law makes \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\) continuous; exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) continuous nearby.  Wasserstein convergence of bounded marginals gives moment convergence, and lem:restricted-marginal-extrema-continuity gives endpoint convergence.  Therefore both endpoint moment matrices converge.  The triangle \(\Omega(\xi_0)\) is positive definite, so it remains uniformly positive definite nearby.

The novel completion is the finite union of compact rank-zero, rank-one, and rank-two factors.  The projector representation makes \(g_B^+(c)\) and \(w^+(B)\) jointly continuous on each fixed-rank factor.  Hence each factorwise optimum value is continuous.  The strict inequalities (1) therefore persist on a relative-open neighborhood, forcing every completion optimizer for either criterion to have rank two.

Optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack also persists.  Otherwise there would be \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) and rank-two completion optimizers whose ordinary preimages have normalized smallest eigenvalue below \(\kappa+\eta/2\).  Compactness gives a convergent subsequence.  Joint continuity makes its limit an optimizer at \(\xi_0\), contradicting the exact slack.  Thus, after shrinking the neighborhood, every completion optimizer has an ordinary preimage in \(\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)\).  Rank-two identification then proves
\[
 \mathcal A_0^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_0(\xi)),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)). \tag{2}
\]

Finally, lem:dominance-gap-lower-semicontinuity and the exact gap at \(\xi_0\) yield a smaller relative-open neighborhood on which \(\Delta(\xi)>\delta/2\).  For every pair of ordinary optimizers the loss difference is at least \(\Delta(\xi)\), hence exceeds \(\delta/2\).  Equation (2) and preservation of loss under \(\iota_\xi\) give the identical conclusion for every pair of completion optimizers. \(\square\)

tldr: Rare network exposures make Horvitz--Thompson estimation noisy, and Zhao's optimal indicator control variates reduce this design variance, but the ex ante basis depends on a cross-world covariance that an unpaired pilot cannot identify. The contribution chain imports the sharp Fréchet covariance range, proves a new fixed-basis affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's objective, poses certified global maximin optimization on the fixed-\(\kappa\) projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency without assuming away ties. Neighborhood persistence is supporting and witness-gated; no strict-dominance region is claimed unless the full-correspondence separation-and-slack certificate is produced.

project_justification.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates explicitly leaves robust basis choice under moment misspecification open; existing Fréchet results identify covariance endpoints, and existing global-optimization results certify Euclidean-box programs, but no paper joins these steps for a block-separable network basis with projective symmetry.
project_justification.niche: Two unpaired pilot marginals identify the exact dependence ambiguity relevant to Zhao's moment matrix while leaving the experimental network and assignment law fixed and known.
project_justification.fill: The project imports the sharp endpoint formulas, proves their affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, formulates a computably specified global maximin certificate on the compact \(\kappa\)-regular projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency. Conditional persistence is supporting: a strict-dominance region requires a separate certified witness with both separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack.

honest_scope: The sharp Fréchet covariance range is imported from AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1. The new theorem targets are its affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, projective compactness, uniform plug-in value and outer-set consistency, and conditional neighborhood persistence. The finite epsilon-global solver and the separated lawful witness are first-class open constructions. Persistence is incremental and yields a strict-dominance region only after the witness supplies both a positive full-correspondence separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack; no such region is otherwise claimed. No SDP reduction, universal minimax interchange, universal strict improvement, asymptotic normality for the pilot-selected basis, or point convergence under ties is claimed.
